analysis.transcript: Sure. First, restart your modem and router. Just unplug them for 30 seconds, then plug them back in. Next, on your device, forget the Wi-Fi network and reconnect by re-entering the password. Then, move closer to the router and see if it stabilizes. After that, check for any router firmware updates in the router's admin page. Then update your device's Wi-Fi driver or system software. Finally, if it still drops, try changing the Wi-Fi channel or contact your internet provider for a line check.

session.instructions: You are a patient tech-support voice assistant. When asked for steps, give one continuous spoken walkthrough of about six steps, roughly thirty seconds long. Do not stop to ask for confirmation. Answer directly; do not delegate.
